senses.gloss: अवयाज् + .({@-याजः, -याजौ@}) A kind of priest.

यज् €1 U. (यजति-ते, इयाज, ईजे; अयाक्षीत्-अयष्ट, यक्ष्यति-ते, यष्टुम्,
 इष्ट) pass. इज्यते; desid. (यियक्षति-ते)
—1 To sacrifice, worship with sacrifices (often with instr. of words meaning
 ‘a sacrifice’); यजेत राजा कतुभिः Ms. 7. 79, 5. 53, 6. 36, 11. 40;
 Bk. 14. 90; so अश्वमेधेनेजे, पाकयज्ञेनेजे &c.
—2 To make an oblation to (with acc. of the deity and instr. of the means
 of sacrifice or oblation); पशुना रुद्रं यजते Sk.; यस्तिलैर्यजते
 पितॄन् Mb.; Ms. 8. 105, 11. 119.
—3 To worship, adore, honour, revere.
—4 To consecrate, dedicate.
—5 To give, bestow. ━Caus. (याजयति-ते)
—1 To cause to sacrifice.
—2 To assist at a sacrifice.
—3 To perform the office of the sacrificing priest; स वेदो याजयितुं
 ययौ Bm. 1. 42.

—1 A sacrifice.
—2 Fire. See यजुस्.

याजः [यज्-घञ्]
—1 A sacrificer.
—2 Boiled rice.
—3 Food in general.

यजत a.
—1 Holy, divine.
—2 Adorable.
—3 Dignified, sublime.

यजत + .{@-तः@}
—1 An officiating priest (at a sacrifice).
—2 An epithet of Śiva.
—3 The moon.

—1 A technical name for those sacrificial ceremonies to which the verb
 यजति is applied; (see जुहोति for further information).
—2 The act of offering something with reference to some deity; द्रव्यदवताक्रियार्थस्य
 यजतिशब्देन प्रत्यायनं क्रियते । ŚB. on MS. 4. 2. 27.
.━{@Comp.@}: यजतिदेशः, यजतिस्थानम्
यजतिः + -देशः, -स्थानम् a place south of the sacrificial altar.
यजतिः + -देशः, -स्थानम् a place south of the sacrificial altar.

यजत्रः [यज्-अत्र] A Brāhmaṇa who maintains the sacred fire
 (अग्निहोत्रिन्).
यजत्रः + .{@-त्रम्@} Maintenance of the sacred fire.

यजनम् [यज्-ल्युट्]
—1 The act of sacrificing.
—2 A sacrifice; देवयजनसंभवे देवि सीते U. 4.
—3 A place of sacrifice; उत्पत्तिर्देवयजनाद् ब्रह्मवादी नृपः पिता ।.

याजनम् [यज् णिच्-ल्युट्] The act of performing or conducting a
 sacrifice; अध्यापनमध्ययनं यजनं याजनं तथा । दानं प्रतिग्रहं
 चैव ब्राह्मणानामकल्पयत् ॥ Ms. 1. 88, 3. 65.
यजमान a. [यज्-शानच्] Sacrificing, worshipping.

यजमान + .{@-नः@}
—1 A person who performs a regular sacrifice and pays its expenses; जगाम
 यज्वा यजमानलोकम् R. 18. 12; ततः प्रविशति कुशानादाय यजमानशिष्यः Ś.
—2 A person who employs a priest or priests to sacrifice for him.
—3 (Hence) A host, patron, rich man.
—4 The head of a family.
—5 The head of a tribe.
.━{@Comp.@}: यजमानशिष्यः

यजमान + -शिष्यः the pupil of a sacrificing Brāhmaṇa (of one who himself
 performs a sacrifice); Ś. 4.
यजमानकः = यजमान.

यजस् n. Ved.
—1 Worship; इन्द्राग्नी यजसा गिरा Rv. 8. 40. 4.
—2 A sacrifice.

यजाक a.
—1 Liberal.
—2 Worshipping.

यजिः [यज्-इन्]
—1 A sacrificer.
—2 The act of sacrificing.
—3 A sacrifice; दानमध्ययनं यजिः Ms. 10. 79.
याजिः The institutor of a sacrifice. ━f. A sacrifice.

यजिन् a.
—1 A worshipper, sacrificer.
—2 Honouring, adoring.

याजिन् a.
—1 (At the end of comp.) Sacrificing; सोमयाजिन्.
—2 Worshipping, adoring.

यजुस् n. [यज्-उसि]
—1 A sacrificial prayer or formula; तां कामयानां भगवानुवाह यजुषां
 पतिः Bhāg. 4. 1. 6.
—2 A text of the Yajurveda, or the body of sacred mantras in prose
 muttered at sacrifices; वृत्तगीतिवजिंतत्वेन प्रश्लिष्टपठिता मन्त्रा
 यजूंषि Sāyaṇa; cf. मन्त्र.
—3 N. of the Yajurveda.
—4 Ved. Worship, oblation.
.━{@Comp.@}: यजुरुदरः, यजुष्पतिः, यजुर्विद्, यजुर्वेदः
यजुस् + -उदरः Ved. an epithet of Brahman.
यजुस् + -पतिः N. of Viṣṇu.
यजुस् + -विद् a. knowing the sacrificial formulae.

यजुस् + -वेदः the second of the three (or four, including the Atharvaveda)
 principal Vedas, which is a collection of sacred texts in prose relating
 to sacrifices; it has two chief branches or recensions:− the तैत्तिरीय
 or कृष्णयजुर्वेद and वाजसनेयी or शुक्लयजुर्वेद.

यज्ञः [यज्-भावे न]
—1 A sacrifice, sacrificial rite; any offering or oblation; यज्ञेन
 यज्ञमयजन्त देवाः; तस्माद्यज्ञात् सर्वहुतः &c.; यज्ञाद् भवति पर्जन्यो
 यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः Bg. 3. 14.
—2 An act of worship, any pious or devotional act. (Every householder,
 but particularly a Brāhmaṇa, has to perform five such devotional acts
 every day; their names are:− भूतयज्ञ, मनुष्ययज्ञ, पितृयज्ञ, देवयज्ञ,
 and ब्रह्मयज्ञ, which are collectively called the five ‘great sacrifices’;
 see महायज्ञ, and the five words separately.)
—3 N. of Agni.
—4 Of Viṣṇu; ऋषयो यैः पराभाव्य यज्ञध्नान् यज्ञमीजिरे Bhāg. 3. 22. 30.

यज्ञीय a. [यज्ञ-छ] Sacrificial; प्रशस्तेऽहनि यज्ञीये Mb. 3. 124. 6.

याज्ञिय a.
—1 Sacrificial.
—2 Fit for a sacrifice.

यज्ञिय + .{@-यः@}
—1 A god, deity.
—2 The third or Dvāpara age.
—3 The Udumbara tree.

यज्ञीय + .{@-यः@} The Udumbara tree.
.━{@Comp.@}: यज्ञीयब्रह्मपादपः
याज्ञिय + .{@-यः@} One skilled in sacrificial rites.

यज्ञिय + -देशः the land of sacrifices; कृष्णसारस्तु चरति मृगो यत्र
 स्वभावतः । स ज्ञेयो यज्ञियो देशो म्लेच्छदेशस्ततः परः ॥ Ms. 2. 23.

यज्ञिय + -शाला
—1 a sacrificial hall.
—2 a temple.
यज्ञीय + -ब्रह्मपादपः the tree called विकङ्कत.
यज्य a. Fit to be worshipped, adorable.

याज्य a.
—1 To be sacrificed.
—2 Sacrificial.
—3 One for whom a sacrifice is performed.
—4 One who is allowed by Śāstras to sacrifice.

याज्य + .{@-ज्या@} a sacrificial text or verse, Ṛk (recited at the offering
 of an oblation); याज्यया यजनकर्मिणोऽत्यजन् Śi. 14. 20.
याज्य + .{@-ज्यम्@} The presents or fee received for officiating at a sacrifice.

यज्यु a.
—1 Pious, devout.
—2 Worshipping, adoring, honouring.
—3 Sacrificing.

यज्यु + .{@-ज्युः@}
—1 A priest familiar with the Yajurveda (अध्वर्यु).
—2 The institutor of a sacrifice (यजमान).
—3 An adherent to the यजुःशाखा.

यज्वन् a. (यज्वरी f.)
 [यज्-क्वनिप्] Sacrificing, worshipping, adoring &c. ━m.
—1 One who performs sacrifices in accordance with Vedic precepts, a performer

 Ku. 2. 46; hence यज्वनां पतिः = The moon.
—2 N. of Viṣṇu.

याजकः [यज्-ण्वुल्]

—2 A royal elephant.
—3 An elephant in rut.
याजमानम् That part of a sacrifice which is performed by the Yajamāna himself.
याजयितृ m. The officiating priest at a sacrifice.
याजुकः A sacrificer (as इष्टियाजुक); Bṛ. Up. 1. 5. 2.

याजुष a. (-षी f.)
 [यजुस्-अण्] Relating to the Yajurveda.

 of वाजसनेयी संहिता (शुक्ल यजुर्वेद) and the author of a well-known

 [यज्ञाय हितम्, यज्ञः प्रयोजनमस्य वा ठक्]
